content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: otel-collector/honeycomb-eu is returning 403 on ingest. Automatic page to oncall.

Ethan: I'm on it. seeing immediate 403 spikes from the honeycomb exporter in EU cluster. I'll gather logs and check vendor status.

Ethan: tail from otel-collector logs:
```
2025-09-12T14:02:11Z ERROR honeycomb_exporter send failed status=403 body=\"{\\\"error\\\":\\\"invalid-api-key\\\"}\" endpoint=https://api.honeycomb.io/v1/otlp  request_id=hnc-9012
2025-09-12T14:02:12Z ERROR honeycomb_exporter send failed status=403 body=\"{\\\"error\\\":\\\"invalid-api-key\\\"}\"
```

Marta: is this new? any deploys lately that touched secrets?

Ethan: no infra deploys in last 2 hours (checked deploy-bot), but I do see a key rotation event in our secrets manager at 13:59 UTC for `honeycomb/eu/otlp` — looks like the rotated key didn't propagate to the DaemonSet env.

Olivia: vendor status page (Honeycomb) looks clean, no incident. I'll open vendor support with correlation id hnc-9012 and ask if they rolled rotationally.

Ethan: mitigation plan: 1) hotpatch collectors with the new key from secret manager, 2) enable local GCS buffering sink for EU collectors, 3) temporarily increase sampling to reduce pressure while backlog flushes, 4) notify customers.

Ethan: hotpatch command to update daemonset env for collectors (will roll gradually):
```bash
kubectl -n telemetry set env daemonset/otel-collector HONEYCOMB_API_KEY=$(vault read -field=value secret/data/honeycomb/eu/otlp) --overwrite
kubectl -n telemetry rollout status daemonset/otel-collector --timeout=3m
```

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: otel-collector rollout started by Ethan (canary=2 pods).

Marta: also add a temporary circuit-breaker so exporters drop immediately on 403s instead of retrying aggressively; that slows down CPU thrashing and reduces duplicate retries.

Ethan: adding policy patch to collector configmap to treat 403 as fatal and emit backpressure metric. Patch applied to canary.

Support Bot: Creating support tickets for customers with high trace dependency in EU region and attaching incident ref INC-2060012345.

Olivia: vendor reply: Honeycomb support says they did a rolling key cleanup earlier today which may invalidate short-lived keys; they asked for timestamps and sample payloads. They haven't flagged platform-wide issues. They suggested reissuing keys and hinted at a small rollout nuance.

Marta: interim customer message suggestion: \"We detected failed trace deliveries to Honeycomb in EU caused by an invalidated API key during a key rotation. We have patched collectors and enabled buffering; most traces will be delivered within 15–45 minutes. If you rely on real-time tracing, you may see delays or gaps.\" Should we post to status.redwood.ai?

Ethan: yes post it. I'll include the mitigation steps and ETA. Also adding internal note: owners=Ethan (postmortem).

Olivia: verification after canary patch: canary pods show 200s to Honeycomb: `2025-09-12T14:07:02Z INFO honeycomb_exporter send ok status=200 req=hnc-9023`

Ethan: rolling patch to remaining collectors now. Monitoring queue length: `otel_queue_len` metric was 18k at peak; after buffer enabled and sampling increased it's down to ~4.2k and draining.

Marta: how much data lost vs delayed?

Ethan: rough estimate using span counts: expected ~1.1M spans in 30m window; observed 0.95M forwarded; approx 13% delayed/dropped — most buffered for later delivery.

Support Bot: Notified affected customers and created follow-up tickets. Account leads pinged.

Olivia: vendor updated: they accepted the sample payloads and reissued guidance. They noted their short-lived key TTL can cause collectors that didn't pick up latest secret to get 403s. They recommended we implement an exponential backoff then fallback-to-buffer pattern.

Ethan: adding follow-ups to runbook: 1) ensure secret-sync cron runs every 30s for critical envs, 2) implement exporter behavior: on 403 treat as credential rotation -> fall back to buffer and alert ops, 3) implement SaaS-key-change dashboard showing secret rotation vs collector uptime.

Marta: are we safe to close the page? vendor says all good from their side, our collectors are healthy, backlog under 500, and customers notified.

Ethan: I'll keep monitoring for 30m, but reporting to close. Postmortem assigned to Ethan; preliminary RCA: key rotation + secret propagation gap + no buffer-fallback behavior in exporter. Follow-ups: change sync period, add buffer-fallback, update playbook, and add alert that correlates 403 bursts with secret-change events.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident transitioned to monitoring. If errors >5% re-open.

Marta: handing off oncall to Olivia for next 60m monitoring.

Olivia: thanks — I'll watch metrics and vendor channel. I'll also draft the longer postmortem and timeline once Ethan has initial notes.

Ethan: posted interim status on status.redwood.ai: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2060012345

Marta: thanks everyone. Closing channel discussion unless vendor re-opens.
